questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether screens affect us differently from books
How to write successful children's books
Why young people have stopped reading
How eye doctors treat problems caused by screens
questions.why: Georgie asks whether reading from screens is harmless or could be damaging us.

questions.q: What do Phil and Georgie have in common?
options: They both read only on paper
They both work as teachers
They both love books but read from screens a lot
They both think screens are better for reading than books
questions.why: Both say they love books, and Phil admits he ends up reading from screens most days.

questions.q: According to Cressida Cowell, what three things does reading bring?
options: Money, fame and friends
Creativity, intelligence and empathy
Speed, memory and focus
Confidence, patience and a sense of humour
questions.why: She says reading brings “three magical powers – creativity, intelligence, and empathy”.

questions.q: What does Cressida say reading for pleasure is linked to?
options: Spending less time with family
Becoming a famous writer
Having better eyesight
Economic success later in life
questions.why: She says it's one of the two key factors in a kid's later economic success.

questions.q: What have researchers found about “deep reading” skills?
options: They can't be taught to children
They develop just as well on screens
They only matter for older students at university
They develop better when children read books
questions.why: Phil says tests show deep reading skills develop better when kids read from books.

questions.q: Why does Professor Wolf mention the cerebral cortex?
options: To explain why screens hurt our eyes
To show that deep reading uses more of the brain
To prove that children read faster than adults do
To describe a brain illness caused by phones
questions.why: She says when we read deeply, we use much more of our cerebral cortex.

questions.q: According to Professor Wolf, what matters most about reading?
options: How we read, rather than what or how much
Reading as many words as possible each day
Choosing only classic books
Reading out loud to others
questions.why: She says it's not what or how much we read, but how we read, that's really important.

questions.q: Why do screens encourage skimming, according to Phil?
options: Because the text on most screens is far too small
Because people read screens only at night
Because we get so many words and notifications
Because screen texts are always short
questions.why: He says it's the volume of words, pings and notifications screens bombard us with.
